description.value: This study examined menstrual-cycle phase-dependent changes in BOLD responses to visual high-calorie, low-calorie, and control food pictures in twelve women using functional MRI.

spans.text: Twelve women underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging during the peri-ovulatory and luteal phases of the menstrual cycle in a counterbalanced fashion.

value: We postulate that ovarian steroid modulation of the corticolimbic brain contributes to changes in ingestive behavior during the menstrual cycle.

description.value: Participants viewed high-calorie food pictures, low-calorie food pictures, and control pictures while being scanned; they were instructed to pay close attention and imagine eating the food.

spans.text: HC food pictures
Subjects viewed pictures of HC foods, LC foods, and control (C) pictures while being scanned.
HC food images consisted of high fat savory foods, such as pasta, red meat, pizza or high fat sweet foods such as cake, cookies and ice cream.
LC food pictures
Subjects viewed pictures of HC foods, LC foods, and control (C) pictures while being scanned.
LC foods consisted of low fat items, such as steamed vegetables, fruit, and grilled fish.
control (C) pictures
Control images were of similar color and complexity and included recognizable objects not associated with eating, such as landscapes, flowers, seashells.

description.value: Functional images were realigned, coregistered with anatomical scans, spatially normalized, and smoothed.

spans.text: Functional images were realigned to the first volume to correct for small movement artifacts after discarding the first three functional images. The functional scans were co-registered with the anatomical scans and spatially normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) EPI template. Images were smoothed with a 6 mm full-width-half-maximum Gaussian kernel to improve the signal to noise ratio without sacrificing spatial resolution.
Scans were preprocessed using Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8; Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, U.K.) software in MATLAB > 7.2 2006.
